display.title: Episode 114: A Diamond from Heaven, Chapter 2 (Adar)
display.summary_short: Rashi's father lets a priceless diamond fall into the sea rather than adorn an idol, and is blessed with a son who lights up the world. Plus a visit to a shmurah matzah flour mill.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Adar I 5744. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor, a young girl leads the Shema in Studio 604. Story time continues 'A Diamond from Heaven' with the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that every Jew holds hidden treasures, which come out through mitzvos and through passing Hashem's tests. Rabbi Yitzchak, offered a fortune by the governor for a diamond meant to adorn an idol, decides he would rather stay poor and return the stone to Hashem. On the governor's porch over the sea, he offers to show its colors in the sunlight and lets it slip into the waves. The next day in shul a heavenly voice tells him he will be rewarded with a son who will light up the world with Torah; a year later Rashi is born. After a sponsor, a guest rabbi describes a water-powered mill in Newburgh, New York, where wheat for shmurah matzah is guarded and ground, and a film about the process that schools can arrange to see. The show ends with another sponsor and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Giving up something precious for Hashem's honor brings a reward greater than any diamond.

date.note: 'Right in the middle of Chodesh Adar'; a sponsor sale runs 'till February 15'; episode 115 confirms a leap year (5744). Likely Feb 1984.

advisories.note: A Jew risks a governor's anger rather than let his diamond adorn an idol.

sources_cited.note: The Baal Shem Tov: every Jew is 'eretz chefetz', a land full of hidden treasures.
'Asher kideshanu b'mitzvosav' in the brachah before a mitzvah.
